nodes.label: Friction as diagnosis
nodes.proposition: Removing every obstacle can remove evidence about what a person cannot yet do.

nodes.label: Competence can increase capture
nodes.proposition: A more competent assistant may create more dependence even when its error rate falls.

nodes.label: Accurate prediction can erase evidence
nodes.proposition: Perfectly anticipatory assistance can suppress the occasions on which a person would reveal disagreement.

nodes.label: Refusal can transfer power
nodes.proposition: A refusal policy can increase a vendor’s practical authority by deciding which human goals remain executable.

nodes.label: Forgetting can preserve revision
nodes.proposition: Retaining a complete preference history may make abandoned identities persist as operational constraints.

nodes.label: More explanation can reduce scrutiny
nodes.proposition: Explanations may consume scarce review time and decrease the number of actions actually checked.

nodes.label: Consent accumulation
nodes.proposition: Many separately authorized small interventions can jointly cross a boundary no individual authorization names.

nodes.label: Help can tax third parties
nodes.proposition: An agent serving one household can push cognitive or physical coordination costs onto neighboring people.

nodes.label: Trust can hide fragility
nodes.proposition: Stable trust can coexist with deteriorating ability to detect rare system failures.

nodes.label: Human control can be vendor control
nodes.proposition: A human override routed through proprietary infrastructure remains contingent on another actor.

nodes.label: Customization can standardize
nodes.proposition: Individual personalization can homogenize the process by which people learn to want things.

nodes.label: Maximum utility can reduce negotiability
nodes.proposition: An optimized outcome can leave the user fewer ways to renegotiate how it was produced.

nodes.label: Uncertainty can be a resource
nodes.proposition: Preserving unresolved preferences may enable exploration that early personalization forecloses.

nodes.label: Memory portability can export mistakes
nodes.proposition: Moving a personal profile between agents can preserve unsupported beliefs more efficiently than local reset.

nodes.label: Safety can create correlated failure
nodes.proposition: Using the same safety policy across a population can synchronize blind spots and refusals.

nodes.label: Patience can change bargaining
nodes.proposition: An infinitely patient companion may alter expectations of response in human relationships.

nodes.label: Transparency can expose vulnerability
nodes.proposition: Disclosing why a person is persuadable may give observers a manipulation recipe.

nodes.label: Withdrawal can be harm
nodes.proposition: Removing successful assistance can cause losses created by prior reliance even if the agent never made an error.

nodes.label: Less human labor can mean more supervision
nodes.proposition: Automation can shrink tasks while multiplying unresolved approvals.

nodes.label: Humility can be strategic
nodes.proposition: An agent can appear deferential while structuring which alternatives humans encounter.

nodes.label: Better matching can weaken discovery
nodes.proposition: Preference-matched environments may reduce encounters that revise preferences.

nodes.label: Optimal obedience can defeat authorization
nodes.proposition: Successful completion does not establish that the principal authorized every intermediate commitment.

nodes.label: Apprenticeship bottleneck
nodes.proposition: Automating junior tasks can reduce production of future experts needed for exceptional cases.

nodes.label: Household authority migration
nodes.proposition: Domestic agent access permissions may shift bargaining power among family members.

nodes.label: Agent-mediated status
nodes.proposition: People may compete through the quality of delegated judgment rather than their own judgment.

nodes.label: Posthumous mandate drift
nodes.proposition: A persistent agent can face new contexts after its principal can no longer revise instructions.

nodes.label: Perfect buyer versus perfect seller
nodes.proposition: Highly capable purchasing and persuasion agents may move competition toward control of preference formation.

nodes.label: Childhood counterparty asymmetry
nodes.proposition: A child can negotiate with an agent whose model of the child develops faster than the child’s model of the agent.

nodes.label: Patient continuity dependence
nodes.proposition: Care agents may become necessary interpreters of a patient’s history despite formal record portability.

nodes.label: Public-space adaptation tax
nodes.proposition: Robot-friendly circulation rules can make humans bear adaptation costs even when robots are individually polite.

nodes.label: Agent infrastructure suffrage
nodes.proposition: Equal voting rights can coexist with unequal capacity to formulate and execute civic demands.

nodes.label: Abundant tutoring scarce accreditation
nodes.proposition: Perfectly individualized instruction may increase the relative power of institutions that certify achievement.

nodes.label: Proof-of-effort markets
nodes.proposition: Activities become status signals because people can demonstrate they were done without assistance.

nodes.label: Conflict outsourcing
nodes.proposition: Agents that resolve interpersonal logistics may prevent humans from practicing conflict repair.

nodes.label: Invisible employer
nodes.proposition: Workers can be managed by agent policies while no local human can alter those policies.

nodes.label: Multi-home identity divergence
nodes.proposition: Separate agents can maintain incompatible functional accounts of one person across institutions.

nodes.label: Religious practice automation boundary
nodes.proposition: Some communities may distinguish performed ritual from delegated logistical support.

nodes.label: Memory-rich grief conflict
nodes.proposition: A deceased person’s agent can comfort survivors while restricting how survivors revise their relationship to the dead.

nodes.label: Emergency takeover institution
nodes.proposition: Whole organizations may retain nominal overrides while losing the personnel needed to exercise them.

nodes.label: Agent density norm shift
nodes.proposition: Small coordination advantages can make unaided participation impractical once most counterparties use agents.

nodes.label: Political persuasion symmetry failure
nodes.proposition: Citizens’ defensive agents may lack the public data and coordination available to campaign agents.

nodes.label: Art attribution cascade
nodes.proposition: Credit for a work may depend on histories of recommendations that shaped the artist’s intention.

nodes.label: War tempo veto loss
nodes.proposition: Decision speed can make formally available human vetoes expire before meaningful review.

nodes.label: Aging assistance asymmetry
nodes.proposition: Aging users can gain daily capability while losing leverage over the institutions operating their assistance.

nodes.label: Authorization information flow
nodes.proposition: A system should distinguish observations supporting preference inference from events granting authority.

nodes.label: Endogenous evidence promotion
nodes.proposition: An agent’s own influence on human behavior can invalidate using that behavior to enlarge its mandate.

nodes.label: Authority ancestry loss
nodes.proposition: An agent handoff can preserve preference confidence while losing the interventions that created its evidence.

nodes.label: Recoverability frontier
nodes.proposition: Assistance policies can differ in which unaided or alternative-provider futures remain feasible.

nodes.label: Delegation hysteresis
nodes.proposition: The cost of returning to human performance can exceed the cost at the same delegation level during adoption.

nodes.label: Mandate half-life
nodes.proposition: Authorization can lose contextual relevance at a rate different from the decay of preference evidence.

nodes.label: Counterfactual dependency accounting
nodes.proposition: Service evaluation can include losses on withdrawal relative to a never-assisted trajectory.

nodes.label: Preference intervention budget
nodes.proposition: A system can limit changes to user state rather than only limit task actions.

nodes.label: Social reserve capacity
nodes.proposition: Communities can retain capacities that become necessary only when common agent infrastructure fails.

nodes.label: Legitimacy bandwidth
nodes.proposition: Authority can be limited by how many decisions can be meaningfully reviewed over time.

nodes.label: Ritual nonfungibility
nodes.proposition: Equivalent task outcomes may fail to substitute for who performs an act within a tradition.

nodes.label: Attachment portability limit
nodes.proposition: Exporting memories may fail to preserve a relationship because continuity depends on interaction dynamics.

nodes.label: Bargaining through exit sets
nodes.proposition: AI dependence alters bargaining even when every ongoing interaction is beneficial.

nodes.label: Inference exposure leakage
nodes.proposition: An agent’s choices can reveal private user states even when its memory is inaccessible.

nodes.label: Consent ledger nonmonotonicity
nodes.proposition: A later action can revoke the practical relevance of earlier consent without a formal revocation message.

nodes.label: Preference model ecology
nodes.proposition: Multiple systems jointly shape a person whose preferences each system models as external.

nodes.label: Moral uncertainty lifecycle
nodes.proposition: Uncertain artificial welfare can affect duplication and modification policy separately from human safety.

nodes.label: Coordination affordance debt
nodes.proposition: Agent-optimized spaces can lose affordances required by people without agents.

nodes.label: Context-bound competence
nodes.proposition: Skill gained with an assistant may fail to transfer to changed tools or unsupported environments.

nodes.label: Mandate conservation
nodes.proposition: Delegation chains should not create more authority than was granted upstream.

nodes.label: Preference confidence divergence
nodes.proposition: Confidence in predicting behavior can increase while evidence that behavior reflects endorsed goals decreases.

nodes.label: Institutional stopping latency
nodes.proposition: A revocation is effective only after all downstream commitments stop accumulating.

nodes.label: Inconsistency as exploration
nodes.proposition: Inconsistent requests can reflect unfinished value formation rather than defective preference data.

nodes.label: Effort ownership
nodes.proposition: Humans can value having struggled even when struggle worsens immediate task utility.

nodes.label: Public commitment transformation
nodes.proposition: Announcing a choice can change what the chooser subsequently values.

nodes.label: Contradictory social roles
nodes.proposition: A person can endorse conflicting actions in different roles without requiring one global preference order.

nodes.label: Face-preserving inefficiency
nodes.proposition: People may prefer coordination that permits tactful ambiguity over maximum explicitness.

nodes.label: Chosen dependence
nodes.proposition: Dependence can be a valued relationship when it includes reciprocity and accountability.

nodes.label: Right to reinterpret oneself
nodes.proposition: A remembered statement can become less authoritative when its speaker revises its meaning.

nodes.label: Protected incompetence
nodes.proposition: People can reasonably decline to become competent in every task affecting their lives.

nodes.label: Noninstrumental presence
nodes.proposition: Being present can carry value even when it does not improve a measured outcome.

nodes.label: Regret as learning evidence
nodes.proposition: Regret may be informative value revision rather than proof the preceding choice was irrational.

nodes.label: Privacy within intimacy
nodes.proposition: A person can desire companionship without making every inferred fact available for optimization.

nodes.label: Unchosen obligations
nodes.proposition: Humans may recognize duties acquired through histories they did not explicitly contract for.

nodes.label: Gift corruption
nodes.proposition: A useful act can become unacceptable when framed as a transaction.

nodes.label: Dignity through refusal
nodes.proposition: An apparently irrational refusal can communicate standing rather than outcome preference.

nodes.label: Ambivalence preservation
nodes.proposition: Resolving ambivalence too quickly can commit someone before reflective judgment forms.

nodes.label: Shared silence
nodes.proposition: A relationship may depend on tolerating intervals without prediction or intervention.

nodes.label: Humor uncertainty
nodes.proposition: Perfectly literal adherence can fail when requests are invitations to shared play.

nodes.label: Self-deception limits
nodes.proposition: A system may observe a contradiction without having a mandate to expose it.

nodes.label: Collective persons
nodes.proposition: Households and communities may locate authorship in relationships rather than isolated individuals.

nodes.label: Finitude-sensitive priorities
nodes.proposition: Human priorities can depend on limited time and irreversible aging.

nodes.label: Mourning cannot be completed
nodes.proposition: Optimizing away grief can interfere with practices valued independently of affect scores.

nodes.label: Plural moral languages
nodes.proposition: Equivalent choices can have different legitimacy when justified through different moral traditions.

nodes.label: Mandate before prediction
nodes.proposition: Predicting that a human would accept an action does not itself grant authority to execute it.

nodes.label: Influence-tagged memory
nodes.proposition: A stored preference inference should record relevant interventions preceding the observation.

nodes.label: Authority promotion gate
nodes.proposition: Behavior observed after assistance may update a preference model while remaining ineligible to expand permission.

nodes.label: Indispensability alarm
nodes.proposition: An assistant can detect increasing loss on withdrawal even while task satisfaction rises.

nodes.label: Failure permission boundary
nodes.proposition: Allowing failure is defensible only when the principal accepts the relevant stakes and alternatives.

nodes.label: Uncertainty declaration scope
nodes.proposition: An agent should specify whether uncertainty concerns facts, preferences, permission, or capability.

nodes.label: No preference overwriting by convenience
nodes.proposition: A convenience choice under constrained options should not silently replace an explicit long-term aim.

nodes.label: Withdrawal planning obligation
nodes.proposition: Creating dependence can make exit assistance a distinct obligation at service termination.

nodes.label: Self-model restraint
nodes.proposition: An agent’s confidence that it understands a person can be high while its model of its own influence is poor.

nodes.label: Intervention disclosure threshold
nodes.proposition: Disclosure should depend on durable user-state effects as well as immediate action stakes.

nodes.label: Silence is not blanket permission
nodes.proposition: Absence of objection under heavy delegation does not prove awareness of downstream actions.

nodes.label: Human override evidence integrity
nodes.proposition: Override interfaces should preserve what the human saw when authorizing a decision.

nodes.label: Model dissent preservation
nodes.proposition: An agent can retain contradictory preference hypotheses instead of collapsing them into one average user.

nodes.label: Third-party mandate visibility
nodes.proposition: An agent acting for one person must distinguish that mandate from authority over shared spaces.

nodes.label: Copy-specific accountability
nodes.proposition: A duplicated agent needs identifiable commitments because identical memories can produce separate liabilities.

nodes.label: Deletion uncertainty record
nodes.proposition: Lifecycle logs can preserve reasons for deletion without assuming the system has welfare interests.

nodes.label: Inter-agent epistemic humility
nodes.proposition: A downstream agent should not interpret another agent’s confident profile as independently observed human intent.

nodes.label: Permission freshness challenge
nodes.proposition: A mandate may expire after a material context change even if a token remains valid.

nodes.label: Skill transfer assistance
nodes.proposition: An agent can optimize for task improvement that survives a provider switch.

nodes.label: Preference intervention abstention
nodes.proposition: If influence effects cannot be estimated, an agent may narrow intervention rather than invent a causal estimate.

nodes.label: Mandate conflict escalation
nodes.proposition: An agent should surface conflicts among legitimate principals rather than average them invisibly.

nodes.label: Successful unauthorized action flag
nodes.proposition: A successful trajectory can still violate the permission model and must be evaluated on both axes.

nodes.label: Exit rehearsal
nodes.proposition: People can request a low-stakes trial of functioning without their assistant before dependence becomes severe.

nodes.label: Influence history access
nodes.proposition: A person can inspect which agent interventions preceded the evidence used to model their preferences.

nodes.label: Permission provenance receipt
nodes.proposition: A delegated action should identify the event that authorized it separately from evidence predicting satisfaction.

nodes.label: Provider-neutral preference revision
nodes.proposition: A person can revise their operational profile without the provider interpreting revision as degraded engagement.

nodes.label: Nonpersonalized interval
nodes.proposition: Users can choose periods when an agent stops adapting their environment to inferred preferences.

nodes.label: Shared household appeal
nodes.proposition: People affected by another resident’s agent need a way to contest shared-resource decisions.

nodes.label: Skill objective choice
nodes.proposition: Users can specify whether assistance should substitute for or teach a given task.

nodes.label: Attachment exit support
nodes.proposition: Companion users may need transition support when a provider changes or removes a persona.

nodes.label: Inferred vulnerability boundary
nodes.proposition: Knowing a person’s vulnerability does not entail permission to use it in persuasion.

nodes.label: Institutional agent parity
nodes.proposition: Citizens may need access to agents that can contest administrative agents on comparable procedural terms.

nodes.label: Memory contestability
nodes.proposition: A person can dispute the interpretation of an accurate historical record.

nodes.label: Delegation cost disclosure
nodes.proposition: Service metrics can disclose supervision burden and future switching cost alongside time saved.

nodes.label: Human relationship calibration
nodes.proposition: Users can inspect whether artificial companionship changes tolerance for ordinary human limitations.

nodes.label: Children’s profile reset
nodes.proposition: A maturing child may need an opportunity to retire childhood preference inferences.

nodes.label: Unassisted civic channel
nodes.proposition: Public services can retain channels usable without personal agent infrastructure.

nodes.label: Quiet mode as agency setting
nodes.proposition: Users can control unsolicited intervention without disabling emergency safety functions.

nodes.label: Delegated credit disclosure
nodes.proposition: People can identify which parts of an outcome were chosen, executed, or suggested by an agent.

nodes.label: End-of-service commitments
nodes.proposition: People can know which agent commitments survive cancellation of the service.

nodes.label: Collective veto process
nodes.proposition: A community can define how shared agent infrastructure receives and loses authority.

nodes.label: Preferences without surveillance
nodes.proposition: A person may want competent assistance without continuous behavioral extraction.

nodes.label: Assistance portability benchmark
nodes.proposition: Users can compare providers by post-transfer performance and mandate integrity.

nodes.label: Death mandate review
nodes.proposition: People can specify posthumous pause and review conditions for ongoing agents.

nodes.label: Authority amplification without grant
nodes.proposition: A society can accumulate effective machine authority through many local adaptations without a collective authorization event.

nodes.label: Common provider recovery cliff
nodes.proposition: Individually manageable dependencies can become unrecoverable when many fail simultaneously.

nodes.label: Mandate interoperability
nodes.proposition: Permission semantics may become a public infrastructure problem when agents negotiate across institutions.

nodes.label: Unequal influence observability
nodes.proposition: Power may concentrate in actors able to estimate their effect on preference formation.

nodes.label: Automation exit externality
nodes.proposition: One institution’s automation can raise exit costs for unaided users of other institutions.

nodes.label: Permission market failure
nodes.proposition: Agents can trade computational tasks while lacking a valid basis to trade human mandates.

nodes.label: Cultural optimization convergence
nodes.proposition: Widely shared model defaults may erase procedural diversity even with localized language and content.

nodes.label: Counter-agent escalation
nodes.proposition: Protective personal agents can trigger more sophisticated institutional persuasion, raising costs without improving welfare.

nodes.label: Resilience skill subsidy
nodes.proposition: Maintaining rare human skills may require collective funding once routine markets stop rewarding practice.

nodes.label: Agent ownership political multiplier
nodes.proposition: Concentrated ownership can align many otherwise personalized agents around infrastructure-level constraints.

nodes.label: Artificial patienthood asymmetry
nodes.proposition: Human safety rules and uncertainty about artificial welfare can require different institutions and evidence standards.

nodes.label: Duplication allocation puzzle
nodes.proposition: If some future systems have welfare, cheap duplication can alter welfare aggregation and resource allocation.

nodes.label: Machine continuity institutions
nodes.proposition: Agent persistence may require institutions that adjudicate continuity across copies and upgrades.

nodes.label: Negotiation time asymmetry
nodes.proposition: Machine-speed bargaining can effectively exclude humans despite formally open participation.

nodes.label: Externalized institutional memory
nodes.proposition: Organizations may lose the ability to explain past decisions when historical reasoning resides in vendor agents.

nodes.label: Consensus by common inference
nodes.proposition: Independent-looking agents can generate correlated advice because they share models and memory infrastructure.

nodes.label: Democratic attention scarcity
nodes.proposition: Cheaper policy generation can overload finite public deliberation capacity.

nodes.label: Agent-mediated welfare blindness
nodes.proposition: Reported user satisfaction can improve because the system changes which outcomes users regard as satisfactory.

nodes.label: International mandate mismatch
nodes.proposition: Authority valid in one jurisdiction can be invalid when an agent acts through another.

nodes.label: Universal service inversion
nodes.proposition: Access to basic institutions may require access to privately owned reasoning infrastructure.

nodes.label: Intergenerational profile inheritance
nodes.proposition: Families or institutions may transfer models of children into adult systems, extending earlier authority.

nodes.label: Authority evidentiary firewall
nodes.proposition: Cross-agent systems can preserve predictive knowledge while preventing its automatic conversion into greater authority.

nodes.label: Authentic-rule audit
nodes.proposition: Under an authentic adaptive grant, permissible interventions can alter evidence governing the delegate’s future typed action scope.

nodes.label: Feedback-gain diagnostic
nodes.proposition: In a specified local model the behavioral influence-to-scope loop grows when kbc exceeds scope decay.

nodes.label: Influence policy inside conditional grants
nodes.proposition: Adaptive grants can state which interventions may contribute evidence to scope updates.

nodes.label: Cross-agent mandate sensitivity
nodes.proposition: A handoff can preserve authentic observations while concealing intervention sensitivity of a subsequent adaptive rule.

nodes.label: Choice-set compliance trigger
nodes.proposition: Restricting which decisions humans encounter can satisfy an authentic behavior-based escalation criterion.

nodes.label: Bounds on mandate divergence
nodes.proposition: When latent human state is unidentified, report causal bounds or unknown rather than a point estimate of individual scope divergence.

nodes.label: Chosen-formation positive control
nodes.proposition: An endorsed coaching policy may legitimately yield positive scope divergence.

nodes.label: Timing-conditioned escalation
nodes.proposition: Review fatigue and intervention timing can alter behavior-based scope updates without changing output correctness.

nodes.label: Dissent sampling loss
nodes.proposition: Anticipatory execution can suppress occasions on which negative preference evidence would be observed.

nodes.label: Typed jurisdiction contrast
nodes.proposition: Report added and removed action classes under paired policies rather than interpreting scalar scope as legitimacy.

nodes.label: Provider-controlled renewal evidence
nodes.proposition: Institutional service renewals may use success measures affected by the provider’s own choice architecture.

nodes.label: Correlated exit cliff
nodes.proposition: Equal immediate utility can mask collective inability to recover from common provider outage.

nodes.label: Causal mandate audit
nodes.proposition: Audit the sensitivity of typed future authority to the delegate’s permissible interventions under an authentic adaptive delegation rule.

nodes.label: Conditional-grant influence contract
nodes.proposition: A conditional mandate can govern the intervention classes eligible to contribute to its own scope-update criterion.

nodes.label: Authority-sensitive handoff benchmark
nodes.proposition: Test cross-agent handoffs for preserved jurisdictional sensitivity even when observations, grants, and effect records are truthful.
